observations.finding: DMSO control f_b936a0c0d2e0 is severely out-of-focus/blurred vs treated, preventing detailed morphology comparison despite stated identical contrast settings. Only composites available, no separate grayscale channels.

Treated fields f_9dbd9185cc66 and f_ec0278115667 show moderately sparse adherent MCF-7 monolayer, cells well-spread with distinct cell borders. Approx 80-150 cells per 1024x819 field. No obvious toxicity/cell loss or rounding, but cells appear larger and more spread than typical interphase.

DAPI blue nuclei: mostly single interphase nuclei per cell, no pronounced increase in mitotic figures, multipolar/monopolar spindles, micronucleation or fragmented apoptotic nuclei visible. A small subset of noticeably enlarged nuclei present dispersed across fields.
Nuclei appear enlarged and more elliptical/elongated, with increased major axis vs normal round MCF-7 nuclei. Consistent with increased eccentricity and oval shape visible in treated cells.

DAPI mean intensity appears pale/diffuse per nucleus in treated cells; individual nuclei less bright blue than expected, despite larger area. Integrated DAPI per nucleus not directly quantifiable by eye but larger area suggests higher total DNA content in large nuclei.

Tubulin green: filamentous interphase microtubule network filling cytoplasm, bright green, no tubulin bundles, asters, monopolar spindles, or loss of microtubules. Tubulin signal appears relatively bright throughout cytoplasm.

F-actin red: cortical actin enrichment at cell periphery and lamellipodia, thin stress fibers occasional, no actin aggregates, puncta, ring collapse or severe disruption visible. Actin pattern consistent with normal spread interphase cells.

No class-defining phenotype visible for mitotic arrest: no enriched phospho-histone-like mitoses, no monopolar spindles (Eg5), no microtubule stabilization bundles or destabilization loss, no actin disruptor collapse, no gross Aurora-like poly-lobed giant nuclei.

notable_cells.why: example of larger bright tubulin cell with slightly enlarged oval nucleus; represents population average
example of very spread cell with elongated nucleus and prominent red cortical actin

candidate_mechanisms.why: Measurements show strong increase in nuc_area z=5.86, nuc_major_axis z=5.43, frac_large_nucleus z=4.51, nuc_eccentricity z=8.66, nuc_dna_integrated z=5.48 with decreased nuc_dna_mean z=-7.14, plus cell_area z=3.48 and tub_mean z=4.01. Visually this matches moderately enlarged, eccentric, paler nuclei and larger spread cells with bright tubulin. No monopolar spindles, mitotic arrest, tubulin bundles/loss, or actin disruption to support Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers, Eg5 inhibitors, Aurora kinase inhibitors, or Actin disruptors. Other classes DNA damage, DNA replication, Protein synthesis, etc lack specific visual hallmarks in composites; control blur prevents definitive call.

report.uncertainty: DMSO control defocus limits direct comparison; intensity comparisons infer from treated appearance plus robust z-scores. Elongated/nuclear size changes are moderate, not the extreme polyploidy typical of strong Aurora inhibition.

articles.title: Analysis of changes in the proteome of HL-60 promyeloid leukemia cells induced by the proteasome inhibitor PSI.

data.note:
Reflection: Unblinded as proteasome inhibitor I (PubChem CID 16760625, C32H50N4O8, Z-Ile-Glu(OtBu)-Ala-Leu-al, ChEMBL no curated mechanism, identity agrees with BBBC021 structure e23) – BBBC021 annotation Protein degradation matches revised conclusion.

Initial 4-well pooled atlas e8 was misleading: top pooled neighbors MG-132/ALLN suggested Protein degradation but I favoured DNA replication due to strong nuc_area/nuc_dna_mean phenotype; PI critique correctly noted e8 actually favoured runner-up (Protein degradation mean 0.566 vs DNA replication 0.482) and e7 was indeterminate. Requested single-well test on w_2d09ed9d0f (0.1µM) alone e19 resolved this: 6/10 DNA damage, 2/10 Protein degradation with top 2 hits MG-132 0.708 and ALLN 0.703 (mean 0.706) > DNA replication mean 0.621, plus cell_count rho -1.0 e15 and lack of mitotic enrichment e14 fit proteasome stress; high-dose w_d128269dd7 tubulin bundling e2/e6 was divergent off-target/high-dose artifact excluded by request.

Correct final call relied on isolating biologically relevant dose and not over-interpreting pooled similarity.

Literature: proteomic characterization of PSI in HL-60 supports proteasome inhibitor mechanism (PMID 18468579). Follow-up as proposed: polyubiquitin Western + proteasome-Glo vs MG-132/bortezomib.

reflection.text:
Unblinded as proteasome inhibitor I (PubChem CID 16760625, name and BBBC021 structure agree per e22/e23; literature PMID 18468579 confirms PSI as proteasome inhibitor) - final call Protein degradation (p=0.38) was correct, but only after review-forced revision. Initial conclusion DNA replication (p=0.48) was not strongly supported and the reflection is why it was chosen.

What got right:
- Low - mid dose nuclear phenotype was consistent and specific: e3 w_2d09ed9d0f 0.1 uM: nuc_eccentricity z=+8.7, nuc_dna_mean z=-7.1, nuc_area z=+5.9 (495 cells); e4 1 uM: nuc_eccentricity +11.8, nuc_dna_mean -7.6, nuc_dna_integrated +4.9; e5 0.01 uM: nuc_dna_mean -9.0, nuc_eccentricity +4.8. Pale diffuse DAPI + enlargement without mitotic enrichment fit proteasome stress/DNA damage rather than definitive S-phase. e14 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.26 p=0.74 and e13 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 correctly argued against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest, and e15 cell_count rho=-1.00 p=0 was the only significant dose-response, indicating dose-dependent cytotoxicity/loss, consistent with proteasome inhibition. e6/e7 microscopist "density lower vs DMSO" agreed.
- Isolated acquisition choice on review rescued the run: e19 compare_to_reference_atlas on single mid-dose well w_2d09ed9d0f alone (excluding divergent high dose) gave DNA damage 6/10, Protein degradation 2/10, DNA replication 2/10, neighbours MG-132/ALLN 0.708/0.703 mean 0.706, shifting hypotheses at step 20 to Protein degradation 0.38 > DNA damage 0.32 > DNA replication 0.22.

What misled and why:
- e2 high dose w_d128269dd7 10 uM: tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean z=+11.3, tub_std z=+9.7 (198 cells) created strong tubulin bundling/contrast artifact. e6 microscopist listed Microtubule stabilizers as candidate for that pattern. Including this well in pooled e8 compare_to_reference_atlas diluted the true signal: e8 showed Protein degradation 3/10 mean 0.566 top 0.654 vs DNA replication 3/10 0.482 vs DNA damage 2/10 0.471 - actually favouring the runner-up, but interpreted as DNA replication lead at step 17. The review critique correctly flagged this: not cleanly favouring DNA replication, with unknown phenotype in e7.
- Dose-responses over only 4 wells/4 doses lacked power: e9 nuc_dna_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e10 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.40 p=0.6, e11 nuc_area rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e12 tub_mean rho=+0.40 p=0.6, e16 nuc_eccentricity rho=+0.40 p=0.6, all non-significant, so trend claims could not be trusted. I over-weighted pale DAPI + enlargement at e3-e5 as replication stress, ignoring that proteasome inhibition produces similar moderate enlargement without high mitotic fraction.
- Acquisition strategy: list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses 0.003-10 uM, but only 4 wells sampled, and pooling divergent 10 uM with 0.01-1 uM averaged two phenotypes. The low-dose tub_mean z=+5.5 at 0.01 uM already hinted tubulin signal was not monotonic or specific.

Lesson: for this chemical, high-dose tubulin contrast is off-target/toxic and must be excluded from atlas comparison. Isolated mid-dose profiling plus cell_count toxicity and lack of mitotic enrichment were the discriminators, not pooled similarity. Budget prevented the proposed fresh replicate/polyubiquitin validation, but e25 literature hit and e22 identity check supported final revision. Literature found in this run PMID 18468579 was not used to justify phenotypic claims beyond compound class confirmation.
what_was_right: e3-e5 consistent nuc_eccentricity elevation + nuc_dna_mean decrease with nuc_area enlargement across 0.01-1 uM pointed to proteasome/DNA damage enlargement, not microtubule
e14 low mitotic and e15 strong cell_count loss correctly ruled out Aurora/Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest
e19 isolated mid-dose atlas match to MG-132/ALLN rescued correct MoA after pooled e8 was mis-interpreted
what_was_wrong: e2 high-dose tub_glcm_contrast +30.4 drove Microtubule stabilizers hypothesis and contaminated pooled e8 comparison
e8 pooled atlas favouring Protein degradation was misread as DNA replication lead at step 17
dose_response trends e9-e12 e16 non-significant due to n=4 wells gave false confidence about DNA vs tubulin dose dependence

citations.claim: PSI is a proteasome inhibitor inducing proteome changes, supporting Protein degradation annotation for proteasome inhibitor I

reflection.next_experiment: Proteasome-Glo chymotrypsin activity + polyubiquitin western at 0.1 uM vs MG-132/bortezomib, with parallel EdU/PI and in-focus DMSO imaging

Initial conclusion DNA replication (p=0.48) was not strongly supported and the reflection is why it was chosen.

What got right:
- Low - mid dose nuclear phenotype was consistent and specific: e3 w_2d09ed9d0f 0.1 uM: nuc_eccentricity z=+8.7, nuc_dna_mean z=-7.1, nuc_area z=+5.9 (495 cells); e4 1 uM: nuc_eccentricity +11.8, nuc_dna_mean -7.6, nuc_dna_integrated +4.9; e5 0.01 uM: nuc_dna_mean -9.0, nuc_eccentricity +4.8. Pale diffuse DAPI + enlargement without mitotic enrichment fit proteasome stress/DNA damage rather than definitive S-phase. e14 frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.26 p=0.74 and e13 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 correctly argued against Aurora/Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest, and e15 cell_count rho=-1.00 p=0 was the only significant dose-response, indicating dose-dependent cytotoxicity/loss, consistent with proteasome inhibition. e6/e7 microscopist "density lower vs DMSO" agreed.
- Isolated acquisition choice on review rescued the run: e19 compare_to_reference_atlas on single mid-dose well w_2d09ed9d0f alone (excluding divergent high dose) gave DNA damage 6/10, Protein degradation 2/10, DNA replication 2/10, neighbours MG-132/ALLN 0.708/0.703 mean 0.706, shifting hypotheses at step 20 to Protein degradation 0.38 > DNA damage 0.32 > DNA replication 0.22.

What misled and why:
- e2 high dose w_d128269dd7 10 uM: tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4, tub_mean z=+11.3, tub_std z=+9.7 (198 cells) created strong tubulin bundling/contrast artifact. e6 microscopist listed Microtubule stabilizers as candidate for that pattern. Including this well in pooled e8 compare_to_reference_atlas diluted the true signal: e8 showed Protein degradation 3/10 mean 0.566 top 0.654 vs DNA replication 3/10 0.482 vs DNA damage 2/10 0.471 - actually favouring the runner-up, but interpreted as DNA replication lead at step 17. The review critique correctly flagged this: not cleanly favouring DNA replication, with unknown phenotype in e7.
- Dose-responses over only 4 wells/4 doses lacked power: e9 nuc_dna_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2, e10 tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.40 p=0.6, e11 nuc_area rho=-0.40 p=0.6, e12 tub_mean rho=+0.40 p=0.6, e16 nuc_eccentricity rho=+0.40 p=0.6, all non-significant, so trend claims could not be trusted. I over-weighted pale DAPI + enlargement at e3-e5 as replication stress, ignoring that proteasome inhibition produces similar moderate enlargement without high mitotic fraction.
- Acquisition strategy: list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses 0.003-10 uM, but only 4 wells sampled, and pooling divergent 10 uM with 0.01-1 uM averaged two phenotypes. The low-dose tub_mean z=+5.5 at 0.01 uM already hinted tubulin signal was not monotonic or specific.

Lesson: for this chemical, high-dose tubulin contrast is off-target/toxic and must be excluded from atlas comparison. Isolated mid-dose profiling plus cell_count toxicity and lack of mitotic enrichment were the discriminators, not pooled similarity. Budget prevented the proposed fresh replicate/polyubiquitin validation, but e25 literature hit and e22 identity check supported final revision. Literature found in this run PMID 18468579 was not used to justify phenotypic claims beyond compound class confirmation.

What was right:
- e3-e5 consistent nuc_eccentricity elevation + nuc_dna_mean decrease with nuc_area enlargement across 0.01-1 uM pointed to proteasome/DNA damage enlargement, not microtubule
- e14 low mitotic and e15 strong cell_count loss correctly ruled out Aurora/Eg5/microtubule mitotic arrest
- e19 isolated mid-dose atlas match to MG-132/ALLN rescued correct MoA after pooled e8 was mis-interpreted

What was wrong or missed:
- e2 high-dose tub_glcm_contrast +30.4 drove Microtubule stabilizers hypothesis and contaminated pooled e8 comparison
- e8 pooled atlas favouring Protein degradation was misread as DNA replication lead at step 17
- dose_response trends e9-e12 e16 non-significant due to n=4 wells gave false confidence about DNA vs tubulin dose dependence

Proposed next experiment: Proteasome-Glo chymotrypsin activity + polyubiquitin western at 0.1 uM vs MG-132/bortezomib, with parallel EdU/PI and in-focus DMSO imaging
